title: Measuring the tug-of-war between two nonlinearities in a monopolar plasma vortex
summary: From planetary atmospheres to magnetized plasmas, single-core vortices organize flows and transport heat and matter. Understanding their persistence requires identifying the nonlinear interactions that sustain a single core. Theories of monopolar drift vortices attribute the additional nonlinearity to either the electron-temperature gradient or density-profile curvature, but their respective roles remain experimentally unresolved. We measure three-wave coupling among the vortex harmonics using simultaneous probe signals acquired around the full azimuth of a laboratory plasma and compare it with predictions of an extended drift-wave equation derived for the measured equilibrium conditions. The equation reproduces the sign, magnitude and triad dependence of the observed coupling without adjustable parameters, whereas neither contribution alone accounts for the measured coupling pattern. This coupling transfers fluctuation power from the linearly driven fundamental to damped harmonics, maintaining the single-core waveform. These results establish an experimental route to distinguishing mechanisms that produce similar vortex structures by resolving the nonlinear interactions within them.

title: Global full-f gyrokinetic analysis of energetic-particle-driven Alfvén eigenmodes and their phase-space drive with GYSELA
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Nuclear Fusion
summary: We investigate the linear stability of energetic-particle (EP) driven Alfvén eigenmodes and the wave-particle interaction in phase space, using the newly implemented energetic-particle module in the electromagnetic global full-f gyrokinetic code GYSELA. The coupled gyrokinetic-Maxwell system self-consistently evolves the EP species alongside thermal ions and kinetic electrons, retaining finite-orbit-width and global profile effects. To mitigate the relaxation of the initial distribution in global full-f models, a canonical Maxwellian initialisation is employed, which strongly reduces this relaxation and the associated change of the drive. The framework is verified against the ITPA-TAE and the reversed-shear NLED-AUG cases, including scans in EP temperature and density. The agreement with published multi-code results is quantitative for the ITPA-TAE case and qualitative for the NLED-AUG case, where a reversed-shear Alfvén eigenmode (RSAE) is found near $q_{\rm min}$. Beyond verification, we use a constants-of-motion (CoM) diagnostic to project the gyrocentre distribution and the local wave-particle power exchange ($P = -\mathbf{J}\cdot\mathbf{E}$) onto invariant space. This identifies the orbit classes and resonances that interact with the mode. For the ITPA-TAE, deeply co-passing orbits dominate the drive. For the NLED-AUG RSAE, counter-passing orbits drive the mode and co-passing orbits damp it, and the sign of the exchange follows that of the linear EP drive. title: The effects of closure parameter on the properties of kinetic range plasma turbulence
summary:
Simulations of plasmas such as the solar wind require an accurate representation of kinetic physics given the lack of frequent collisions. Fully kinetic treatments are computationally expensive and necessarily confine simulations to small domain sizes. A good compromise is to utilise higher-order fluid-moment models such as the 10-moment model.
  This model retains all physics up to the second moment, with the moment hierarchy closed by approximating the heat flux.
  One choice is to use a model for the divergence of the heat flux, $\partial_m q_{ijm} \approx v_t |k_0|(\mathbf{P}_{ij}-pδ_{ij})$, with a free parameter $k_0$, called the ``closure parameter''. We study the effects of this closure parameter on the properties of turbulence, combined with artificial ion-electron mass ratios. We show that the heating of the two plasma species is affected by the choice of the closure parameter. For all combinations of closure parameters, the relative compressive and incompressive heating rates are affected even for realistic mass ratios. The effects are more prominent for lower mass ratios and diminish when approaching realistic mass ratios.

AI.tldr: The paper studies how the free closure parameter in a 10-moment fluid model, together with artificial ion-electron mass ratios, affects heating and turbulence properties in kinetic-range plasma turbulence.
AI.motivation: Fully kinetic simulations of weakly collisional plasmas such as the solar wind are computationally expensive and limited to small domains, so higher-order fluid-moment models are used as a compromise. The heat-flux closure in such models introduces a free parameter whose influence on turbulence is unclear.

title: Streaming instabilities and electron transport in electron transpiration cooling
summary: Electron transpiration cooling requires emitted electrons to travel through a surrounding plasma, where their relative motion with background electrons can drive streaming instabilities. Lower neutral densities show pronounced wave activity, while higher densities give smoother electron distributions. A multifluid model constructed from simulated velocity distributions captures the frequency scale and decay direction in selected cases, but underestimates the separate driving and absorbing responses of electron populations. Distinguishing fast and slow emitted electrons and normalizing the field amplitude by the expanding two-peak length improves the low-wavenumber growth comparison, while discrepancies remain. Spatial growth estimates show that finite propagation distance also limits amplification. Strong late-time current fluctuations can coexist with nearly complete mean anode collection. These findings connect streaming instability to electron transport in the cooling model and show both the usefulness and limitations of a fluid description.

title: Toward divertor plasma detachment in pure D-T plasma in fusion reactor with H-mode-like plasma confinement
summary: The conditions between the separatrix plasma density and the heat flux into the scrape-off layer region allowing reaching an ultimate divertor plasma detachment with H-mode confinement in pure hydrogen (deuterium or the mixture of deuterium and tritium) plasma are obtained. title: Exact force-free three-dimensional toroidal equilibria and the sawtooth q(0) problem
summary: We construct exact, closed-form solutions of curl of B=lambda B with nested toroidal flux surfaces around a closed magnetic axis, finite rotational transform and, in general, no continuous Euclidean symmetry. The rotational transform is a ratio of one-dimensional integrals. Our primary application is the sawtooth q(0) problem in tokamaks. In one configuration, q crosses unity on a smooth torus of closed field lines, with no island and no current sheet. Across the family, minimum-energy fixed-boundary states with q(0)<1<q_wall exist; in our scans q(0) reaches 0.84 at tight aspect ratio and about 0.94 at conventional aspect ratio. At comparable helicity-to-flux ratio, configurations with different boundary shapes have either sign of the magnetic shear. These fixed-boundary equilibria are candidates for relaxed cores, which need not be axisymmetric. Their dynamical accessibility and their matching to the surrounding plasma remain open.

summary: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

AI.tldr: Particle-in-cell simulations show that ion heating in high-Mach-number collisionless shocks correlates with X-type magnetic structures downstream, suggesting magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by large-amplitude Alfvén waves contributes to ion–electron energy partitioning.
AI.motivation: The partitioning of energy between ions and electrons in collisionless shocks remains unresolved. Large-amplitude Alfvén waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front are especially important in high-Mach-number shocks, motivating an examination of both conventional wave–particle heating and preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection in current sheets formed by Alfvén-wave trains.
AI.method: The study uses particle-in-cell simulations to investigate large-amplitude Alfvén waves and the current sheets they form, focusing on ion heating and its relationship to magnetic field structures in the downstream shock region.
AI.result: The simulations reveal a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region. The authors suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence energy partitioning between ions and electrons. Quantitative heating efficiencies and partition fractions are not provided in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic reconnection within current sheets associated with large-amplitude Alfvén waves is proposed as an additional mechanism affecting ion heating and ion–electron energy partitioning in collisionless shocks.

title: CHORD: Learning Latent Spaces for Constrained Stellarator Design
summary: In high-dimensional, PDE-constrained design, interpolating between known feasible solutions can reveal trade-offs without repeating expensive optimization campaigns. In stellarator design for fusion energy, direct interpolation of plasma boundary parameters can violate physical constraints even when both endpoints are feasible. Learned latent representations can capture nonlinear relationships among design variables, but latent interpolation can still cross infeasible regions, and conditioning on target metrics can become inconsistent with the decoded design. We introduce CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training, paired with self-consistent inference that aligns conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. Geometric benchmarks show the benefit of regularizing latent interpolants. In stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, CHORD reaches up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility, compared with 50% for an unregularized conditional VAE and 28% for direct interpolation of boundary parameters. Ablations show that both ingredients are needed for this gain. Beyond interpolation, latent-space optimization finds simulator-feasible designs, while self-consistent sampling produces more diverse feasible alternatives. On the ConStellaration benchmark, chord-regularized models with linear conditioning reuse data from five optimization campaigns and simulator-labeled rescalings to populate the Pareto front more densely. After low-fidelity screening, 93% of 1.2k generated candidates pass the benchmark's high-fidelity feasibility test. We release code and over 600k designs for stellarator generation, surrogate training, and front-filling evaluation. These results support feasibility-aware latent learning for exploring constrained design trade-offs.

AI.tldr: CHORD is a conditional variational autoencoder for constrained stellarator design that regularizes decoded latent interpolants against predicted constraint violations and uses self-consistent inference to align target-metric conditioning with decoded designs. It improves simulator-validated feasibility for interpolation and supports feasible design optimization, diverse sampling, and denser Pareto-front filling.
AI.motivation: High-dimensional PDE-constrained design is expensive, and interpolating between feasible stellarator plasma boundary parameters can violate physical constraints. Learned latent representations capture nonlinear design relationships, but latent interpolation can still cross infeasible regions, and conditioning on target metrics can become inconsistent with the decoded design.
AI.method: The authors introduce CHORD, a conditional variational autoencoder that penalizes predicted constraint violations along decoded latent interpolants during training. It is paired with self-consistent inference that aligns conditioning with the decoded design's predicted metrics. The method is evaluated on geometric benchmarks, stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, latent-space optimization, self-consistent sampling, and the ConStellaration benchmark, with ablations of both components.
AI.result: CHORD reaches up to 81% simulator-validated mid-segment feasibility for stellarator interpolation between distinct geometry families, versus 50% for an unregularized conditional VAE and 28% for direct boundary-parameter interpolation. Ablations show both ingredients are needed. Latent-space optimization finds simulator-feasible designs, and self-consistent sampling produces more diverse feasible alternatives. On ConStellaration, chord-regularized models with linear conditioning reuse data from five optimization campaigns and simulator-labeled rescalings to populate the Pareto front more densely; after low-fidelity screening, 93% of 1.2k generated candidates pass the high-fidelity feasibility test. Code and over 600k designs are released.

title: Making Reconnection Cooler: A relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics model for radiative collisionless reconnection
summary: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely site for particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has substantially modelled such collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force countering the acceleration of the particles. Here, we systematically derive an energy-momentum sink term in relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription which reproduces the fast reconnection rate seen in kinetic calculations, to model radiative losses. We show that our radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties -- including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the out-flowing plasma -- for inverse Compton cooling applied to two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmarked to kinetic simulations. Our results hold in various cooling regimes with a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory. Our radiative model lays a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, such as in reconnection sites in a local turbulent flow or globally in the magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a kinetic-informed radiative energy-momentum sink term for relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), couples it to a charge-starved resistivity prescription, and shows that two-dimensional RRMHD simulations with inverse Compton cooling reproduce key kinetic reconnection properties across cooling regimes.
AI.motivation: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely source of particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has modeled collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force, motivating a systematic RRMHD treatment of radiative losses that remains consistent with kinetic results.
AI.method: The authors derive an energy-momentum sink term in RRMHD informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription that reproduces the fast reconnection rate found in kinetic calculations. They apply inverse Compton cooling in two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmark the results against kinetic simulations.
AI.result: The radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties, including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the outflowing plasma. The results hold across various cooling regimes and show a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory.
AI.conclusion: The radiative model provides a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, including reconnection sites in local turbulent flows and global magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.
